reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap record in Aulla, Italy, tagged as a data center, is more plausibly a small fixed-wireless ISP's equipment site than an AI compute facility.

The record carries zero megawatts, no operator, and no confirmed business registration. Its name, Wi-Fi Communication Aulla, points to a wireless internet provider, and the reading places it in the Lunigiana area of Tuscany, where wired broadband is less developed and fixed-wireless service is common. The physical form implied is a base station or network operations point supporting backhaul and management, which is real telecom infrastructure but a different business from commercial colocation.

For AI specifically, this matters as a boundary case. The binding constraints on AI scaling are power and buildings, and a facility with no stated megawatt capacity and no colocation function does not relieve either. Counting it as data center capacity would overstate what exists.

What the data does not tell the reader is anything confirmed. The operator website is listed but was not verified, and the research status is exhausted, meaning the entry rests on a single OpenStreetMap tagging review from 2026-09-04. The nearest airport, Sarzana-Luni, is 8.4 miles away, which says nothing about compute. This is one unconfirmed point, not a measure of Italian data center capacity.
